TwentyNoteRef.description:
Where this transcript ended up in Twenty.

`CANONICAL` — this recording's content became the CRM note.
`SECONDARY` — a teammate recorded the same meeting and their note won; we
deliberately did NOT create a second note in the client's CRM, and point at
theirs instead. The user can override this from the UI if the overlap test
got it wrong (two genuinely different meetings with the same company).

canonicalTranscriptId.description: Set when role is SECONDARY: the transcript that actually produced the note.

RecordingWindow.description:
Capture window as measured by the recording client.

`Transcript.recordedAt` is the UPLOAD time and `durationSeconds` is derived
from the last utterance — neither is the true meeting start. Two teammates
recording the same call upload at different moments, so comparing those
fields alone is unreliable. When the client reports these, overlap detection
uses them instead.

startedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant capture actually started.

wallClockSeconds.description: Wall-clock seconds from start to stop (includes pauses, unlike durationSeconds).

speakers.description: AI insights per speaker (name inference + summary + sentiment + speaking time).

speakerNameOverrides.description:

re-applied after any reprocess so human fixes survive fresh AI passes.

links it back to the pain point (resolutionTaskId) + the transcript, and

that already has a resolution task returns 409.

Generate (or regenerate) the Project Digest: a living synthesis of ALL the
project's meetings — decisions, open action items, recurring themes,
history and next steps. Reuses docGenerationService (the digest is a
DocDocument, themed with the project's theme). Confidential meetings are
excluded. The resulting doc id is stored on Project.metadata.digestDocId.

put.description:

reprocessing via metadata.speakerNameOverrides.

post.description:
Retry a single failed post-meeting task (Jira sync, Google Drive export,
doc generation, etc.) without rerunning the entire transcript pipeline.
Returns immediately; the caller observes the status transition via
`metadata.postMeetingTasks.{kind}` on the next transcript poll.

Receives updates from the Telegram Bot API for the "Berry" sales bot.

Unauthenticated by necessity (Telegram has no OAuth for webhooks) — the gate
is the `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header registered via `setWebhook`,
following the same shape as the Stripe and GitHub receivers in this codebase.

Answers 200 immediately and processes in the background: Telegram retries
any update it doesn't get a prompt response for, and generation takes far
longer than its tolerance — without this a slow generation becomes a
duplicate-proposal loop.
